title: Police open probe into simultaneous AI-driven bank hacks in South Korea
key_facts: On 2 Oct 2026 the Korean National Police Agency's Cyber Terror Response Investigation Unit opened a preliminary inquiry into simultaneous information leaks across the banking sector.
The inquiry covers banks where hacking damage was officially confirmed that day, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank and BNK Busan Bank.
Chosunbiz describes the leaks as a string of artificial intelligence (AI) hacking attacks on major commercial banks.
Police moved as soon as the damage was reported in the media and plan to set up an investigative framework quickly.
If the inquiry becomes a formal investigation, it would be the first major cyber case police handle after the revised Criminal Procedure Act took effect on the same day (2 Oct 2026).
The new Serious Crimes Investigation Agency (SCIA) also launched on 2 Oct and counts hacking among its seven major serious crimes, but was not yet able to start an investigation.
quote_evidence: According to police on the 2nd, the Korean National Police Agency's Cyber Terror Response Investigation Unit launched a preliminary inquiry that day in connection with the simultaneous information leak incidents across the banking sector.
The targets are financial institutions where hacking damage was officially confirmed that day, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, Hana Bank, and BNK Busan Bank.
Police moved as soon as the damage was reported in the media.
why_it_matters_hint: Police have stepped in after hacking damage was confirmed at several major banks at once.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (police inquiry and official confirmation of damage)
notes: Short article (about 1,350 characters). It gives no number of customers and no kind of data leaked, and 'AI hacking attacks' is Chosunbiz's own description.
